guideTitle: 5 Best Large Print Keyboards for Mac (2026)
metaTitle: Best Large Print Keyboards for Mac (2026)
metaDescription: Five large print keyboards for Mac compared on key contrast, backlighting, layout and connection, for readers who struggle with small legends.
mainKeyword: best large print keyboards for mac
introParagraphs: A large print keyboard for Mac makes the letters bigger and the contrast stronger, which helps anyone who squints at standard keycaps or types in a dim room. The five keyboards here take different routes to readability. The Logickeyboard Astra2 uses backlit white letters on black keys with five brightness levels, the BERGUF is a full-size 104-key Mac-only board with white backlit characters, the Macally is a compact wired mini with dual USB-C and USB-A connections, the HXMJ uses yellow keycaps in a Bluetooth mini, and the Azio is a washable IP66 board with a three-color LED.

The spread in layout and connection is wide. The BERGUF includes a numeric keypad, the Macally and HXMJ drop it to save space, and the HXMJ connects by Bluetooth up to about 10 meters while the others are wired. Contrast schemes differ too: white on black for the Logickeyboard and BERGUF, black on yellow for the HXMJ, and large print with a colored backlight on the Azio.

We evaluated each keyboard on legend size and contrast, backlighting quality, layout and Mac compatibility, and how well the keys suit tired or stiff hands, based on product specs and buyer feedback. Since the common marketing claim of four times larger lettering is unverified, we favored boards whose listings describe their contrast and backlighting concretely.

products.name: Macally Large Print Backlit Keyboard for Mac
products.description:
The Macally is designed specifically for Mac, with a dual connector that plugs into either a USB-C or a USB-A port. High-contrast large print characters aim to improve visibility and reduce eye strain. Adjustable backlighting helps in dim rooms while keeping a clean look.

The compact mini layout saves desk space. The tradeoff is that a small board has no full numeric keypad, so number entry is slower, and a wired cable limits placement. It sits at a lower cost tier.

Wired connection means no batteries and no pairing, which is the simplest setup for a Mac. Compared with the BERGUF, the Macally is smaller and has dual connectors, while the BERGUF has a keypad. We rank it first because it balances readability and simplicity.
products.bestFor: A simple, wired large print Mac keyboard

products.name: BERGUF Backlit Large Print Keyboard for Mac
products.description:
The BERGUF is a full-size 104-key wired keyboard with a numeric keypad. Oversized white characters on each key and a white LED backlight are designed to give dramatically better visibility. It uses a US QWERTY layout.

The listing is explicit that it is exclusive to Apple computers and does not support Windows. The tradeoff is size, since a full-size board takes more desk room, and the backlight is white only. It sits at the lowest cost tier.

The keypad suits anyone who types numbers, such as for budgeting. Compared with the Macally, it is larger but has the keypad. We would choose it for a home desk with plenty of space.
products.bestFor: Number entry and a full-size layout at low cost

products.name: HXMJ Large Print Mini Bluetooth Keyboard
products.description:
The HXMJ uses bright yellow keycaps with crisp large black letters, a high-contrast scheme that some low-vision users find easier than white on black. It connects by Bluetooth to a MacBook, iPad or iPhone. Operating distance is up to 10 meters.

Silent scissor keys with a metal support make typing quieter and more durable. The tradeoff is that it is a mini board with no keypad, and the listing gives no backlight. Bluetooth needs pairing and charging attention.

It sits at a lower mid-range tier. Compared with the Macally, the HXMJ is wireless and works across Apple devices but is not backlit. We would choose it for someone who types on an iPad as well as a Mac.
products.bestFor: Wireless typing across Mac and iPad
pros: Yellow keycaps with large black print
Bluetooth works with Mac, iPad and iPhone

products.name: Azio KB540 Large Print LED Keyboard Mac Version
products.description:
The Azio KB540 is a Mac version large print keyboard that you can wash. It is rated IP66, which shields it against spills, oils and cleaning agents. A silver-based antimicrobial agent is added to the exterior parts to prevent microbe growth.

A three-color LED backlight improves visibility. The tradeoff is the premium cost, since waterproofing is a niche feature, and color choice can add complexity. It uses a wired USB connection.

It suits shared spaces where a keyboard is cleaned often. Compared with the Macally, it is far easier to sanitize but costs more. We would choose it for a household where spills are common.

products.name: Logickeyboard Astra2 Large Print Backlit for Mac
products.description:
The Logickeyboard Astra2 is designed for people with visual impairments or who have a hard time reading small print. White letters on black keys form a strong contrast, and backlighting is adjustable in five levels. It is described as the most powerful backlit vision keyboard in its range.

The backlight lets you work in dimmed rooms. The tradeoff is that it is the highest cost tier. It is also specialist equipment aimed at low-vision users.

It is made for Mac, so there is no compatibility guesswork. Compared with the BERGUF, the Astra2 offers five backlight levels and vision design but costs much more. We would choose it for strong visual impairment.
cons: Fewer details on connection in the listing

buyingCriteria.explanation: The common marketing claim of four times larger lettering is unverified, with one guide suggesting two to four times. Compare real contrast instead. White on black suits the Logickeyboard and BERGUF, while the HXMJ uses black on yellow, which some makers say is easier. Pick the scheme your eyes read fastest.

Backlighting helps in dim rooms but needs adjustable brightness to avoid glare. The Logickeyboard offers five levels, the Macally adjustable lighting and the Azio a three-color LED. Some models reset to a default color at power-up. Avoid RGB models with flashing effects, which can disorient light-sensitive users.

The BERGUF has a full 104 keys with a numeric keypad, while the Macally and HXMJ are minis. A keypad helps with numbers but takes room. Slightly spaced keys can reduce accidental double presses for arthritic hands.

Wired boards like the Macally and BERGUF avoid battery concerns. The HXMJ uses Bluetooth, which pairs with more devices but needs charging. Some models offer both USB-C wired and Bluetooth. Choose wired if you want zero setup.

The BERGUF is Mac only and does not support Windows, and the Azio is a Mac version. The Macally is made for Mac. Check that function and modifier keys map to macOS. A Windows layout can leave Command and Option keys mislabeled.
A light, consistent key press and bold legends help if arthritis is a concern. The HXMJ uses silent scissor keys. The Azio can be washed, which suits shared use. Try keys in person if you can.

howWeEvaluated.title: Backlight control

howWeEvaluated.title: Layout and connection
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared full-size and mini layouts and wired versus Bluetooth connections. The Macally's dual connector and the HXMJ's Bluetooth each have benefits. The simplest connection scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mac fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked that each was made for or labeled for Mac. The BERGUF and Azio are Mac specific. Strong compatibility scored higher.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value for the tier
howWeEvaluated.description: A higher tier needed a clear benefit such as vision design or washability.

faq.q: Are large print keyboards compatible with Mac?
faq.a: Only if made for Mac. The BERGUF is Mac only and the Azio and Macally are Mac versions. Check the Command and Option keys.

faq.q: Which keyboard has the best contrast?
faq.a: White on black like the Logickeyboard works well, and black on yellow like the HXMJ suits some users. Try both if possible. Contrast preference is personal, so check the return policy if you cannot try the keys first.
It helps in dim rooms. Choose adjustable brightness to avoid glare. Avoid flashing RGB effects.
Wired avoids batteries and pairing. Bluetooth pairs with more devices but needs charging. Choose by your setup.

faq.q: Do I need a numeric keypad?
faq.a: Only if you enter many numbers. The BERGUF has one. The mini boards save space.

faq.q: Can I just use an overlay?
faq.a: Large print overlays are an inexpensive option for an existing keyboard. A dedicated board has better contrast and backlighting. An overlay keeps your existing key feel, which some people prefer, but it can wear or slip over time.
